transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-07
Time: 10:00 PDT / 17:00 UTC
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Jonah, Priya, Leo, Sam, Avery + company-wide dial-in

Summary (auto): Leadership update on platform health, roadmap handoff for Q2, sprint retrospective highlights, hiring snapshot, and ops asks.

Topics: roadmap handoff; reliability & SLOs; Dedicated capacity pricing experiment; Private deployment updates; hiring momentum; customer signals; OKR alignment.

00:00 Speaker Maya: All right, hi everyone, thanks for joining. We're gonna try to keep this tight, got a lot to cover. Quick housekeeping — recording is on, slides will be posted. I want to start with two minutes on context, then hand to Priya for the Q2 product handoff.

01:12 Speaker Priya: Great, thanks Maya. Good morning, afternoon, wherever you are. So for Q2 our primary product theme is "consumption predictability" — that is making costs and latency predictable across hosted, dedicated, and private. We heard from a lot of customers last quarter that unit economics are the blocker for expansion, so the features we prioritize should move the needle there.

02:35 Speaker Jonah: Quick thing on that, Priya — engineering flagged a potential tradeoff on continuous batching aggressiveness; if we push it too far you get lower p99 but higher p50 variability for short requests. We need the product to support per-route batching knobs.

03:18 Speaker Leo: Yeah, we prototyped route-level batching controls in the sandbox last sprint; it's promising but we need more observability. Avery, do we have token-level cost by route surfaced yet?

03:42 Speaker Avery: Not fully — basic breakdown exists but not linked to dashboards. I'll own tying the token-cost view into per-route traces. We'll aim for an example in the Console by the end of next week.

04:55 Speaker Sam: From customer success, the ask is clear: show them the math. Customers want to see how quantization + caching impacts $$ per 1M tokens for their specific workload. If we can show a reproducible example for a few archetypes — chatty, batch embedding, and rerank — adoption will accelerate.

06:10 Speaker Priya: Ok so roadmap bullets: 1) Per-route batching + UI toggles (MVP) 2) Token-level cost dashboards 3) Canary rollout primitives + automatic fallback to cheaper variant 4) Private deployment region expansion for EU and APAC 5) Eval-based quality monitoring for regressions. We'll post the deck.

07:42 Speaker Maya: Thanks. Two managerial snapshots: hiring is strong in infra and product ops, slower in growth. We closed offers for three infra engineers; starting dates staggered in May. Also want to call out the incident from last month — good postmortem, team — but we need a shorter blameless exec summary for customers. Sam, can CS synthesize a one-page?

08:50 Speaker Sam: Yeah we'll draft a customer-facing exec summary and attach the postmortem appendix. Target EOD Tuesday.

09:32 Speaker Jonah: On the incident, technical detail — root cause was an edge-case in "KV cache" eviction under bursty sequences plus a path in the runtime that didn't validate cache metadata after quantized kernel swaps. Fix is in, but we're adding additional regression tests. We're also going to add a small metric to flag any unexpected cache drops in realtime.

11:14 Speaker Leo: Ops update: dedicated pools autoscaling — the policy we shipped last sprint reduces cost but has some pod-churn noise on GPU reclaim. We're tuning the grace periods; also exploring fast-warm GPU options for short lived bursts.

12:02 Speaker Priya: Can we please keep the API contract stable? I want engineering to be deliberate about any field changes. Breaking change windows only in sprints with communication windows.

12:35 Speaker Jonah: Agreed. We'll standardize versioning docs in the Console.

14:00 Speaker Maya: Customer signals — a couple of larger customers are evaluating Dedicated capacity for predictable SLA, and three startups signed up for Private trials. The asks are heavy on SSO/SAML, audit logs, and KMS integrations. Sam, legal has the SOC2 pack ready?

14:45 Speaker Sam: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II reports and a compliance bundle. We'll publish a redacted bundle for trials. For KMS, engineering's integration docs need a little polish.

16:12 Speaker Avery: On encryption and KMS, Private deploys will support HSM in the next cadence, but that's gated on a vendor cert and some networking hardening.

17:30 Speaker Audience (random): question about model catalog — will you add more quantized variants?

17:45 Speaker Priya: Absolutely. We're curating model variants with quantization profiles. We'll add metadata about expected throughput and quality delta per quantization profile in the catalog.

19:22 Speaker Jonah: Technical note — when we present quantization numbers, include the prompt/seq-length distribution. Otherwise it's misleading. Also note that some kernels behave differently at long context lengths.

20:50 Speaker Maya: Ok quick retrospective: what went well last quarter, what didn't, and what we learned. Priya, you start.

21:10 Speaker Priya: Wins — Dedicated pilot launched, Console latency graphs improved, more customers in trials. Misses — rollout cadence slipped on canary tooling, and our eval regressions surfaced late. Learning: we need an eval gating step in the release pipeline.

23:15 Speaker Leo: From engineering, wins are greater test coverage in the runtime, and better infra cost signals. Misses: recruitment lag for senior infra leads. We're doubling down on hiring agencies and internal referrals.

25:02 Speaker Jonah: Also, the kernel-selection heuristics did not generalize across all hardware; we're building a small compiler hook to log decisions and apply ML-assisted choices later.

26:50 Speaker Sam: CS learning: customers love transparent pricing tests. When we shared a sample benchmark for a customer archetype, conversion to Dedicated increased. So more artifacts like that.

28:30 Speaker Maya: Two leadership asks: 1) Ops — reduce mean time to detection; 2) Product — reduce friction for customers to try Dedicated. We'll measure both in OKRs.

30:05 Speaker Audience (Engineer): question about on-prem support matrix — will there be an air-gapped installer?

30:20 Speaker Jonah: We plan an air-gapped installer for late Q3; currently Private supports VPC peering and restricted egress. We'll publish a matrix in the docs.

32:00 Speaker Priya: Quick demo of the new Console mockups for per-route controls — (screen share noise) — so here's the toggle, here's the histogram, and here's a simulation of cost savings. Note: it's a mock so numbers are illustrative.

34:40 Speaker Maya: Nice. Any cross-functional needs to make that happen?

35:01 Speaker Avery: Observability needs a standard event schema; that will make incident correlation easier.

35:25 Speaker Leo: Engineering needs a clear contract on what product will ship in the UI; let's finalize by next Wednesday.

36:10 Speaker Priya: We'll finalize the contract; Priya to own.

37:55 Speaker Audience (People Ops): hiring update — total headcount plan now 172 by end of Q2, still on track. We need interviewers for infra panel.

38:30 Speaker Maya: Please sign up, managers. We're also doing a small leadership offsite in late May for strategy deep-dive. Invite to follow.

39:10 Speaker Sam: Back to customers — pricing experiment idea: offer a short-term discounted burst for Dedicated to prove IO, with telemetry collection. Thoughts?

40:05 Speaker Jonah: Risk is capacity pressure; we should cap it. Also auto-fallback to hosted variant if capacity exausts (exhausts).

41:20 Speaker Maya: Ok good. Priya, build an experiment brief with guardrails and expected metrics.

42:00 Speaker Priya: Will do.

44:05 Speaker Leo: Ops FYI: we're increasing retention on key traces to 90 days for debugging; this will cost a bit, so we need exec signoff.

44:38 Speaker Maya: Approve for now, but Sam please include chargeback guidance for CS.

46:00 Speaker Audience (Engineer): question about model rollbacks and automatic fallback — how do we detect quality regressions automatically?

46:30 Speaker Priya: We're expanding eval suites and tying prompt-sets to production traffic; if a metric crosses threshold we'll auto-fail a rollout. Thresholds will be configurable per customer for Private.

48:05 Speaker Jonah: Implementation detail — we need a low-overhead scoring hook in the runtime to compute quality signals without adding latency.

49:20 Speaker Avery: Observability will provide a sampled stream to make that practical.

51:00 Speaker Maya: Time for lightning announcements and shout-outs.

51:15 Speaker Priya: Shout-out to infra team for the kernel fixes; huge improvement on edge-case throttles.

52:00 Speaker Leo: Kudos to CS for the SOC2 bundle turnaround.

53:10 Speaker Maya: And a reminder about the all-hands surveys — please fill them out. 

54:00 Speaker Audience (random): question — will there be a public roadmap?

54:25 Speaker Maya: We'll keep major themes public but not dates. Product will publish a high-level roadmap doc with themes and investment areas.

55:40 Speaker Priya: Ok final recap and explicit next steps: Priya post roadmap; Leo run latency sweep; Avery link cost dashboards; Sam publish incident exec summary and SOC2 bundle; People Ops finalize hiring plan.

57:01 Speaker Maya: Great. We'll keep this short — last thing: focus on predictable, observable inference. If we can make unit costs predictable for customers, that unlocks a lot. Thanks everyone.

58:12 Speaker (end of meeting): Outro and recording stop.

Notes about transcription: intermittent overlapped talk at minute ~30 and ~51 caused some speaker attribution errors; proper nouns like "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cash" and "HSM" sometimes shown as "H S M". Occasionally product names are paraphrased.

References & artifacts shared: link: https://redwood-internal.company/slides/springboard-q2-deck (posted after meeting), quick benchmark csv: link: https://redwood-internal.company/benchmarks/q2-sample.csv, postmortem: https://redwood-internal.company/incidents/2026-03-kv-eviction-pm

End of transcript.
